simple.meaning: מָרַק (mâraq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to polish ; by implication, to sharpen ; also to rinse.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Leviticus, 2 Chronicles, Proverbs, Jeremiah, beginning at Leviticus 6:21. Its contexts include family, offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָרַק (H4838).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: to polish ; by implication, to sharpen ; also to rinse
definitions.full: H4838. maraq I. [ מָרַק ] verb scour, polish (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic מְרַק ; compare Arabic scrape off wool from a skin); — Qal Imperative הָֽרְמָחִים מִרְקוּ Jer 46:4 polish the lances! Passive participle מָרוּק 2Chr 4:16 polished , of bronze utensils of temple (= מְמוֺרָט 1Kin 7:45 ). Hiph`il Imperfect 3feminine singular חַמְרִיק only Prov 20:30 Kt, figurative, in clause ת מֶּצַע ׳חַבֻּרוֺת בְּרָ֑ע blows that cut in, cleanse away evil (compare De Now Wild VB); Qr תַּמְרוּק i.e. (are) a cleaning . ( ᵐ5 συναντᾷ κακοῖς , whence Gr תַּקְדִּים , Frankenb. תִּקְרֶינָה , but improbable). Pu`al Perfect וּמֹרַק consecutive Lev 6:21 be well scoured , of bronze vessel (|| בַּמָּ֑יִם וְשֻׁטַּף ).
